hasDescription.value: Discerning consumers seeking single-origin, micro-lot coffees scoring 80+ on SCA scale. Values transparency, direct trade, and artisanal roasting. Willing to pay USD 15-50/kg for exceptional lots.
Largest segment worldwide. Purchases pre-ground supermarket coffee or frequents chain cafes like Starbucks and Dunkin. Values consistency, brand recognition, and convenience over origin specificity.

hasDescription.value: Traditional espresso culture. Prefers dark roast, full body, persistent crema. Italian-style bars serving standing espresso. Lavazza, Illy, Segafredo are reference brands.
Subset of specialty focused on estate/farm-level traceability. Prefers pour-over, AeroPress brewing to highlight origin character. Often subscribes to roaster delivery services.
Ready-to-drink canned and bottled coffee. Japan pioneered with UCC and Boss Coffee. US market led by Starbucks bottled Frappuccino. Cold brew RTD is fastest-growing sub-segment.
Hotels, restaurants, cafes, offices, vending. Bulk purchasing with price-quality balance critical. Contract-based supply with consistency requirements.

hasDescription.value: Dominant in markets where convenience trumps quality. Freeze-dried and spray-dried formats. Nescafe holds ~50% global market share. Growing premium instant segment (specialty soluble).

hasDescription.value: Invests in equipment: pour-over drippers, AeroPress, home espresso machines, precision grinders. Buys whole-bean from local roasters. Follows brewing ratios and water temperature protocols.
Purchasing driven by Fair Trade, Rainforest Alliance, Organic certifications. Willing to pay 10-30% price premium for verified social and environmental impact.
Single-serve systems: Nespresso (40% capsule market), Keurig K-Cup, Dolce Gusto. Convenience-driven but increasingly sustainability-conscious (recycling programs).

hasRegion.value: Central Highlands: Dak Lak, Lam Dong, Gia Lai, Dak Nong

hasDescription.value: World's largest Robusta harvest. Vietnam produces 28-32 million bags/year, 95%+ Robusta. Used primarily for instant coffee and espresso blends. Rapidly growing specialty Arabica from Da Lat.
High-altitude washed Arabicas known for bright acidity. Honduras is largest Central American producer. Guatemala Antigua and Costa Rica Tarrazu are benchmark origins.

hasRegion.value: Guatemala, Honduras, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Nicaragua

hasDescription.value: Smallholder-dominated (95% of production from gardens under 1 hectare). Increasing specialty recognition for clean, bright highland coffees. Sigri and Goroka estates are benchmark producers.
Secondary harvest (mitaca/traviesa) enabling Colombia to ship fresh coffee year-round. Smaller volume but often higher cup quality from slower cherry maturation.
Renowned for bright, complex, blackcurrant-like acidity. Auction system at Nairobi Coffee Exchange. Graded by bean size: AA (screen 18+), AB, PB (peaberry). Small fly crop May-July.

hasRegion.value: Sidamo, Yirgacheffe, Guji, Jimma, Harrar, Limu

hasDescription.value: Birthplace of Arabica coffee. Wild and semi-forest grown. Ethiopian Commodity Exchange (ECX) manages trading. Yirgacheffe and Guji naturals command highest premiums.
Unique wet-hulled processing creates distinctive earthy, herbal profile. Sumatra Mandheling and Gayo are premium grades. Java and Sulawesi produce washed Arabica.
Principal harvest (cosecha principal) producing the majority of Colombian coffee. Wet-processed in small farms (fincas). FNC manages quality control through Almacafe.

hasRegion.value: Minas Gerais, Sao Paulo, Espirito Santo, Bahia

hasDescription.value: World's largest coffee harvest. Brazil produces 55-65 million bags/year. Cerrado and Mogiana regions produce premium naturals. Mechanized harvesting common in flat terrain.

hasRegion.value: Cajamarca, San Martin, Junin, Cusco, Amazonas

hasDescription.value: Major organic coffee producer (top 5 globally). Smallholder farms at 1,200-2,000m altitude. Growing specialty reputation. Fair Trade and organic certifications widespread.

Industry-standard market analysis indicator; used in trade agreements

hasDescription.value: Online auction of national competition-winning coffees. Highest prices ever paid for green coffee. Lots scored 87+ by international jury.

hasRelevance.value: Used by all Arabica traders globally; basis for differential pricing

hasDescription.value: The global benchmark for washed Arabica coffee. Most-referenced price in the coffee industry. Delivery months: March, May, July, September, December.

hasDescription.value: Named-origin coffees with traceability. Sold through specialty retailers and premium cafes. Starbucks Reserve, Peet's single-origin tier. Growing segment driven by third-wave influence.
Competition-quality coffees with detailed farm/lot provenance. Sold through specialty roasters, subscription services. Transparent pricing and direct trade relationships common.

Santos Premium, Bourbon Santos, Chiapas Altura, Cerrado Natural

hasDescription.value: Largest revenue segment. Branded supermarket coffee and chain cafe offerings. Blend of origin coffees with consistent flavor profiles. Lavazza, Folgers, Maxwell House price range.
Entry-level coffee segment. Dominated by Robusta blends and lower-grade Arabica. Supermarket store brands, bulk vending coffee. Focus on volume and cost efficiency.
